==Problem==

A scanning code consists of a <imath>7 \times 7</imath> grid of squares, with some of its squares colored black and the rest colored white. There must be at least one square of each color in this grid of <imath>49</imath> squares. A scanning code is called <imath>\textit{symmetric}</imath> if its look does not change when the entire square is rotated by a multiple of <imath>90 ^{\circ}</imath> counterclockwise around its center, nor when it is reflected across a line joining opposite corners or a line joining midpoints of opposite sides. What is the total number of possible symmetric scanning codes?

<imath>\textbf{(A)} \text{ 510} \qquad \textbf{(B)} \text{ 1022} \qquad \textbf{(C)} \text{ 8190} \qquad \textbf{(D)} \text{ 8192} \qquad \textbf{(E)} \text{ 65,534}</imath>

==Solution 1==

Draw a <imath>7 \times 7</imath> square.

<cmath> \begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
K & J & H & G & H & J & K \\
\hline
J & F & E & D & E & F & J \\
\hline
H & E & C & B & C & E & H \\
\hline
G & D & B & A & B & D & G \\
\hline
H & E & C & B & C & E & H \\
\hline
J & F & E & D & E & F & J \\
\hline
K & J & H & G & H & J & K \\
\hline
\end{tabular} </cmath>

Start from the center and label all protruding cells symmetrically. (Note that "I" is left out of this labelling, so there are only 10 labels, not 11, as ending in K would suggest.)

More specifically, since there are <imath>4</imath> given lines of symmetry (<imath>2</imath> diagonals, <imath>1</imath> vertical, <imath>1</imath> horizontal) and they split the plot into <imath>8</imath> equivalent sections, we can take just one-eighth and study it in particular. Each of these sections has <imath>10</imath> distinct sub-squares, whether partially or in full. So since each can be colored either white or black, we choose <imath>2^{10}=1024</imath> but then subtract the <imath>2</imath> cases where all are white or all are black. That leaves us with <imath>\fbox{\textbf{(B)} \text{ 1022}}</imath>.

There are only ten squares we get to actually choose, and two independent choices for each, for a total of <imath>2^{10} = 1024</imath> codes. Two codes must be subtracted (due to the rule that there must be at least one square of each color) for an answer of <imath>\fbox{\textbf{(B) }1022}</imath>.


Note that this problem is very similar to the 1996 AIME Problem 7 https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/1996_AIME_Problems/Problem_7.

==Solution 2 (Very Intuitive and Fast)==

<asy>
size(100pt);
draw((0,0)--(8,0),linewidth(0.5));
draw((0,2)--(6,2),linewidth(0.5));
draw((0,4)--(4,4),linewidth(0.5));
draw((0,6)--(2,6),linewidth(0.5));
draw((2,6)--(2,0),linewidth(0.5));
draw((4,4)--(4,0),linewidth(0.5));
draw((6,2)--(6,0),linewidth(0.5));
draw((0,0)--(0,8),linewidth(0.5));
draw((0,8)--(8,0),dashed+linewidth(0.5));
</asy>

Imagine folding the scanning code along its lines of symmetry. There will be <imath>10</imath> regions which you have control over coloring. Since we must subtract off <imath>2</imath> cases for the all-black and all-white cases, the answer is <imath>2^{10}-2=\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 1022.}</imath>

==Solution 3==

<cmath> \begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
T & T & T & X & T & T & T \\
\hline
T & T & T & Y& T & T & T \\
\hline
T & T & T & Z & T & T & T \\
\hline
X & Y & Z & W & Z & Y & X \\
\hline
T & T & T & Z & T & T & T \\
\hline
T & T & T & Y & T & T & T \\
\hline
T & T & T & X & T & T & T \\
\hline
\end{tabular} </cmath>

There are <imath>3 \times 3</imath> squares in the corners of this <imath>7 \times 7</imath> square, and there is a horizontal and vertical stripe through the middle. Because we need to have symmetry when the diagonals and midpoints of the large square is connected, we can create a table like this: (Different letters represent different color choices between black and white)

<cmath> \begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
A & B & C \\
\hline
B & D & E \\
\hline
C & E & F \\
\hline
\end{tabular}</cmath>
(Note that coloring one <imath>3 \times 3</imath> square will also determine the colorings of the other <imath>3</imath> because the large <imath>7 \times 7</imath> square must look the same when it is rotated by <imath>90^\circ</imath>)

There are <imath>6</imath> different letters and <imath>2</imath> choices of color (black and white) for each letter, so there are <imath>2^6=64</imath> colorings of a proper <imath>3 \times 3</imath> square. Now, all that's left are the horizontal and vertical stripes. Using similar logic, we can see that there are <imath>4</imath> different letters, so there are <imath>2^4=16</imath> different colorings. Multiplying them together gives <imath>16 \times 64 = 1024</imath>. Going back to the question, we see that "there must be at least one square of each color in this grid of <imath>49</imath> squares." We must then eliminate <imath>2</imath> options: an all-black grid and an all-white grid. <imath>1024-2= \boxed{\textbf{(B)} 1022} \\ \phantom{}</imath> 
-hansenhe

==Solution 4 (Similar to Solution 2)==

A symmetric code following the second and third conditions (diagonal and straight lines of symmetry) will automatically fulfill the first one. We can work with the grid by splitting it into different categories: the center (C), the diagonals across the corners (D), the straight lines across the midpoints (S), and the remaining cubes (R) as shown in the diagram below.

<cmath> \begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
D & R & R & S & R & R & D \\
\hline
R & D & R & S & R & D & R \\
\hline
R & R & D & S & D & R & R \\
\hline
S & S & S & C & S & S & S \\
\hline
R & R & D & S & D & R & R \\
\hline
R & D & R & S & R & D & R \\
\hline
D & R & R & S & R & R & D \\
\hline
\end{tabular}</cmath>

If we account for symmetry, we will only need to pay attention to a small section:

<cmath> \begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
D &   &   &   \\
\hline
R & D &   &   \\
\hline
R & R & D &   \\
\hline
S & S & S & C \\
\hline
\end{tabular}</cmath> 

Note: this shows part of the full grid

There are <imath>2^3</imath> states of D, R, and S, and there are 2 states of C so <imath>2^3 \cdot 2^3 \cdot 2^3 \cdot 2</imath> and subtracting 2 cases for all white and all black will bring <imath>2^{10} - 2 = \boxed{\textbf{(B)} 1022}</imath> as our answer.

~Polyline
